annotation.authors_or_issuer: Berg, J.; Gmyrek, P. (International Labour Organization)
key_provisions_or_claims: Generative AI more likely to transform knowledge workers' tasks than eliminate jobs.
Between 644 and 997 million jobs worldwide are knowledge work (19.6-30.4% of employment).
Invisible data-labelling workers face precarity and psychosocial risks needing OSH regulation.
Tripartite social dialogue should guide technology adoption, with social protection and active labour market policies.
Invest in digital literacy and infrastructure to reduce the digital divide.
annotation.summary_en: ILO policy brief (captured via a podcast page) on how ChatGPT and LLMs affect knowledge work. It argues task transformation is likelier than mass job loss, stresses job quality and invisible data-labelling workers, and recommends social dialogue, social protection, adapted labour regulation, and digital literacy and infrastructure investment.
annotation.title_clean: Automation hits the knowledge worker: ChatGPT and the future of work
